premeditation_planning: Yes, the court found premeditation and planning as part of the conspiracy
motive: Fear of losing control over the affairs of the temple and financial irregularities
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence of the last-seen theory, the place of murder and disposal of the body, the recovery of the dead body, the disclosure made by accused no. 3 about the location where the dead body was dumped, the conduct of accused no. 3 in misleading the investigating agencies, the burning of the vehicle used in the commission of the crime, the false insurance claim, the strong motive for the murder, and the criminal conspiracy.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses by considering their evidence in conjunction with other circumstantial evidence, and found that their testimony was credible and supported the prosecution's case.
post_offence_conduct: Accused no. 3 set the car on fire and took it to the garage of PW13, then filed a false insurance claim which was rejected by the insurance company.

appeal_history.high_court: Acquitted accused no. 4 and commuted death sentence to life imprisonment
appeal_history.supreme_court: Dismissed appeals, upheld High Court's conviction

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused, particularly Nos. 1-5, conspired to kidnap and kill the Chairman of the temple due to his intention to transfer them for misappropriation of funds. The evidence included the last-seen theory, the disposal of the body, the recovery of the body, and the conduct of the accused, all pointing to their involvement in the crime.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution's case was based on imagination and that there were other persons hostile to the deceased. They also claimed that the prosecution failed to prove the disproportionate assets of the accused and that the evidence was insufficient to establish guilt.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that conspiracy is rarely hatched in the open and can be inferred from the basic facts and circumstances proved beyond all reasonable doubts, excluding any other conclusion except that of the accused's complicity.

[1962] Supp 2 SCR 830; State of Maharashtra v Daliu 2000 (6) SCC 269; H.P. sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the courts found the accused's involvement in the crime to be inescapable, with strong evidence of conspiracy, motive, and execution of the crime, leaving no manner of doubt about their guilt.
